target: AG1's claim that making Election Day a national holiday would remove scheduling barriers and increase voting access for the overall workforce
objection: A federal holiday designation does not by itself force private employers to close or give paid leave, so many private-sector workers would still face the same work-schedule barriers and the policy would not reliably remove those barriers.

target: AG1's assumption that a holiday would help the people most blocked from voting
objection: Low-income workers are disproportionately in hourly retail, service, and similar jobs with little flexibility and may not be able to take unpaid time off, so they would be especially likely to remain unable to vote even if Election Day were a holiday.

target: AG1's broader claim that a national Election Day holiday is an effective way to increase turnout
objection: Research shows that an election holiday by itself is not an effective strategy for increasing voter turnout compared with other voting-access reforms.

target: AG1's rebuttal that a national holiday could be paired with employer time-off requirements and therefore would not disadvantage low-income workers
objection: A federal holiday still does not itself require private employers to provide paid time off, and retail/service workplaces would likely remain open, so the policy would still not reliably remove work-schedule barriers for many private-sector workers.

target: AG1's claim that early voting and mail/absentee options mean an Election Day holiday would help low-income workers
objection: Even with early in-person or mail/absentee voting, workers may still need to take time on specific days, handle logistics, or meet deadlines, so the holiday does not reliably eliminate the practical access problem for low-income hourly workers.

target: AG1's claim that a holiday helps because it gives time for registration and ballot-access prerequisites
objection: Many registration and ballot-access prerequisites have deadlines before Election Day, so a holiday on Election Day does not reliably help with tasks that must be completed earlier.

target: AG1's claim that Election Day holiday time can help voters complete registration and ballot-access steps
objection: Some prerequisites depend on outside offices, documentation, or processing that takes more than one day and is not sped up by simply having Election Day off, so a holiday cannot reliably eliminate those bottlenecks.

target: AG1's claim that holiday time lets voters complete deadline-sensitive registration and ballot-access tasks
objection: Even when voters have time to prepare forms, the limiting factor may be receipt and processing by election officials, postal systems, or government offices, and holiday-related reduced operations can delay that chain rather than fix it.

target: AG1's claim that federal-holiday closures and reduced hours give low-income voters usable time to complete registration and ballot-access steps
objection: Holiday closures do not automatically create usable time for low-income parents or workers, because many private employers still do not have to provide paid leave and families may lack childcare, so the day may not be practically available for voting-related tasks.
